nameStory: Closterium dianae takes its genus name from the Greek word 'kloster,' meaning spindle, referring to its distinctive crescent or spindle shape. The species name 'dianae' honors Diana, the Roman goddess of the hunt and moon, likely chosen because this tiny algae's curved form resembles a crescent moon.
description: Closterium dianae is a microscopic single-celled green algae that lives in freshwater environments throughout New England. **[UNCERTAIN: Specific morphological details]** Like other members of its genus, it has a distinctive crescent or banana-like curved shape when viewed under magnification. These tiny organisms are typically only visible to the naked eye when they form dense populations that create greenish films or clouds in water.
